questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.e: Use “has lived” with “since” for an action that began in the past and continues.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: If it will rain, we stay inside.
If it rains, we will stay inside.
If it rains, we stayed inside.
If it rained, we will stay inside.
questions.e: After “if” for a real future possibility, use the present: “if it rains”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: They played when the bell was ringing yesterday.
They were play when the bell rang.
They were playing when the bell rang.
They was playing when the bell rang.
questions.e: Use the past continuous for the ongoing action and the past simple for the event.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He use to walked to school.
He was used walk to school.
He used to walk to school.
questions.e: Use “used to” plus the base form for a past habit.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.e: After “have”, use the past participle: “eaten”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Awa is more tall than Mariama.
Awa is as taller than Mariama.
questions.e: For a short adjective, use “-er than”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: You should to drink more water.
questions.e: After “should”, use the base verb without “to”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: There is too many people in the room.
There are too much people in the room.
There be too many people in the room.
There are too many people in the room.
questions.e: Use “are” with plural “people” and “many” with countable nouns.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.e: Use “have + past participle” for the present perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The letters sent yesterday by him.
questions.e: In the passive past, use “were + past participle” for plural “letters”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She enjoys to read after class.
questions.e: After “enjoy”, use a verb ending in “-ing”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: We arrived to the station on time.
We arrive at the station last night.
We arrived in the station on time.
We arrived at the station on time.
questions.e: Use “arrive at” for a specific place such as a station.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I was cooking while my brother was studying.
I cooked while my brother study.
I was cooking while my brother studying.
I were cooking while my brother was studying.
questions.e: Use “was/were + -ing” for two actions happening at the same time.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She works here since three years.
She has worked here for three years.
She have worked here for three years.
She has work here for three years.
questions.e: Use “for” with a length of time and “has worked”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: This is the more interesting book in the library.
This is the interestingest book in the library.
This is the most interesting book in the library.
This is most the interesting book in the library.
questions.e: For a long adjective, use “the most” to form the superlative.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: You must to wear a helmet when you ride.
You must wearing a helmet when you ride.
You must wore a helmet when you ride.
You must wear a helmet when you ride.
questions.e: After “must”, use the base form of the verb.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Although it was late, they continued working.
Although it was late, but they continued working.
Although it late, they continued working.
Despite it was late, they continued working.
questions.e: Use “although” without adding “but” in the same clause.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where I live yesterday.
He asked me where do I lived.
questions.e: In a reported question, use statement word order: “where I lived”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The food is prepared now by them being.
The food are being prepared now.
The food is being prepared now.
The food is been prepared now.
questions.e: For an action happening now in the passive, use “is being + past participle”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.e: “Neither” is singular here, so use “is”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She is interested in learning English.
She is interested to learn English.
She is interested for learning English.
questions.e: After “interested in”, use a noun or an “-ing” form.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: We will meet after the lesson will end.
We will meet after the lesson ends.
We meet after the lesson ended tomorrow.
We will meet after the lesson ending.
questions.e: After “after” for a future event, use the present simple.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: There were a lot of noise outside.
There was a lot of noise outside.
There be a lot noise outside.
questions.e: “Noise” is uncountable, so use “a lot of” and singular “was”.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: If I have more time, I would learned Wolof.
If I had more time, I will learned Wolof.
If I would have more time, I learned Wolof.
If I had more time, I would learn Wolof.
questions.e: For an unreal present situation, use “if + past” and “would + base verb”.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly describes yesterday?
o: Awa went to the market yesterday.
Awa go to the market yesterday.
Awa has go to the market yesterday.
Awa going to the market yesterday.
questions.e: Use the past form “went” for a finished action yesterday.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses “since”?
o: She lived here since 2020 and still does.
questions.e: Use “since” with the starting point of an action that continues.

questions.q: Which sentence describes an action in progress when rain began?
o: They played when it was start to rain.
They were play when it started raining.
They were playing when it started to rain.
They are playing when it started to rain.
questions.e: Use past continuous for the ongoing action and past simple for the event.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly completes the conditional?
o: If you will study, you pass the exam.
If you studied, you will passed the exam.
If you study, you passed the exam.
If you study, you will pass the exam.
questions.e: Use present simple in the if-clause and “will” in the result.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses “already”?
o: We have already finished our work.
We already have finish our work.
We have finish already our work.
We has already finished our work.
questions.e: “Already” commonly appears between “have” and the past participle.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly compares two people?
o: Moussa is more taller than his brother.
Moussa is taller than his brother.
Moussa is tallest than his brother.
Moussa is tall than his brother.
questions.e: Use “taller than” for a comparison between two people.

questions.q: Which sentence gives advice?
o: You should to wear a helmet when you ride.
You should wearing a helmet when you ride.
You should wear a helmet when you ride.
You should wore a helmet when you ride.
questions.e: Use the base form of a verb after “should”.

questions.q: Which sentence uses “much” correctly?
o: There isn't a few sugar left.
questions.e: Use “much” with an uncountable noun such as sugar.

questions.q: Which sentence uses “each” correctly?
questions.e: “Each” takes a singular noun and a singular verb.

questions.q: Which sentence completes “I look forward to…”?
o: I look forward to see you.
I look forward to seeing you.
I look forward to saw you.
questions.e: In this expression, “to” is a preposition followed by a gerund.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly reports the question?
o: She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where do I lived.
She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where was I live.
questions.e: Reported questions use statement word order.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect?
o: I never have be to Saint-Louis.
I have never went to Saint-Louis.
I has never been to Saint-Louis.
I have never been to Saint-Louis.
questions.e: Use “have” plus the past participle “been”.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the correct preposition for clock time?
o: The bus arrives at eight o’clock.
The bus arrives in eight o’clock.
The bus arrives on eight o’clock.
The bus arrives by eight o’clock every day at.
questions.e: Use “at” with a precise time.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a countable expression correctly?
o: There is a few apples in the basket.
There are a few apples in the basket.
There are much apples in the basket.
There are a little apples in the basket.
questions.e: Use “a few” with plural countable nouns.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses the present simple after “when”?
o: Let me know when he will arrives.
Let me know when he arrive yesterday.
Let me know when he arrives.
Let me know when does he arrives.
questions.e: Use the present simple for a future time clause.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly compares speaking skills?
o: She speaks English more better than I do.
She speaks English best than I do.
She speaks English gooder than I do.
She speaks English better than I do.
questions.e: “Better” is the comparative form of “well”.

questions.q: Which sentence makes a polite request?
o: I would like some water, please.
I would like any water, please.
I like some water yesterday, please.
questions.e: Use “would like” plus a noun for a polite request.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly states a possible result?
o: If it will rain, we stay at home.
If it rains, we will stay at home.
If it rains, we stayed at home tomorrow.
If it raining, we will stay at home.
questions.e: Use the first conditional for a possible future result.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly describes last night?
o: We do our homework last night.
We have do our homework last night.
We did our homework last night.
We were did our homework last night.
questions.e: Use the past form “did” with a finished time.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses a superlative?
o: This is one of the better book in the library.
This is one of best books in the library.
This is one of the most best books in the library.
This is one of the best books in the library.
questions.e: Use “one of the” plus a plural noun and superlative.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly describes a place of birth?
o: This is the village where I was born.
This is the village which I was born.
This is the village where I born.
This is the village when I was born.
questions.e: Use “where” to refer to a place.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses “for” with a duration?
o: He has worked here since five years.
He has worked here for five years.
He works here for five years and still does.
He has work here for five years.
questions.e: Use “for” with a length of time.

questions.q: Which sentence agrees with “neither of the answers”?
o: Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither of the answers is correct.
questions.e: “Neither” is singular in this construction.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses a phrasal verb?
o: Please fill the form up before you leave it in.
Please fill in to the form before you go.
Please fill the form with before leaving.
Please fill in the form before you leave.
questions.e: “Fill in a form” means complete it.
